newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine, British businessmen set up council.
newsitem.headline: Philippine, British businessmen set up council.

text.p: The formation of a Philippine-British Business Council, comprising private businessmen, was announced in Manila on Wednesday by British minister of state for trade and industry Lord Fraser.
The council was formed to promote business and investment between the two countries by improving contacts, Fraser told reporters after the formal opening.
Fraser said he hoped the council, which would improve contacts between businessmen in the two countries, will raise the level of trade and investments between the United Kingdom and the Philippines.
A statement issued on the occasion said the UK was among the Philippines' top investors this year.

January to April 1996 preliminary statistics from the Philippine Central Bank show Britain as the second top investor, with total capital inflow amounting to $696.71 million, of which $639.12 million was portfolio investment, and $57.59 million direct equity, the statement said.

"I have been most impressed by the continued growth rates the Philippines has experienced in recent years ... We are telling UK industry, now is the time to be developing your business strategy towards the Philippines," Fraser said.
